FN-OD8FWM-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 60
Committee: Finance and Taxation Education Sponsor: Senator April Weaver
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 04/19/2023
Senate Bill 60 as reported by the Committee on Finance and Taxation Education allows the
Alabama Board of Nursing to annually increase the maximum annual loan amount for loans
provided under the Alabama Loan-Repayment Program for Advanced-Practice Nursing by up to
5% annually for loans provided in years 2 through 4. This could increase the obligations of the
Education Trust Fund by an undetermined amount dependent upon the increase, if any, in the
maximum annual loan amount set by the Board, and the number of loans distributed for years 2
through 4. In addition, this bill replaces the current penalty provisions for defaulting or failure to
honor a contract, from a penalty amount ranging from 20% to 100% of the total principal
amount of the loans, and now provides for a penalty amount equal to 20% of the total amount of
loans received by the participant. Per the Board, the annual average amount of penalties
collected by the Board totals $45,000. This bill will also increase the administrative obligations
of the Board by an undetermined amount to work with the Alabama Commission on Evaluation
Services (ACES) to develop, track, and collect performance metric data and other measures of
success to include in their annual reporting requirements established pursuant to this bill

FN-OD8FWM-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 60
Committee: Finance and Taxation Education Sponsor: Senator April Weaver
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 04/18/2023
Senate Bill 60 as introduced allows the Alabama Board of Nursing to annually increase the
maximum annual loan amount for loans provided under the Alabama Loan-Repayment Program
for Advanced-Practice Nursing by up to 5% annually for loans provided in years 2 through 4.
This could increase the obligations of the Education Trust Fund by an undetermined amount
dependent upon the increase, if any, in the maximum annual loan amount set by the Board, and
the number of loans distributed for years 2 through 4. In addition, this bill could decrease
receipts to the Board by an estimated $45,000 a fiscal year by removing the mandatory penalties
for default or failure to honor the contract.

FN-OD8FWM-3
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 60
Committee: Ways and Means Education Sponsor: Senator April Weaver
Analyst: Tiffany Weaver Date: 05/08/2023
Senate Bill 60 as passed the Senate could increase the obligations of the Education Trust Fund
by an undetermined amount dependent upon the difference in the maximum loan amounts
provided under the Alabama Loan-Repayment Program: (1) as set by the Alabama Board of
Nursing under current law based on in-state tuition increases; and (2) the amounts set by the
Board of up to a 5% increase annually, as provided by this bill.
In addition, this bill would replace the current penalty provisions for defaulting or failure to
honor a contract from a penalty amount ranging from 20% to 100% of the total principal amount
of the loans, under current law, to an amount equal to 20% of the total amount of loans received
by the participant, as provided by this bill. Per the Board, the annual average amount of
penalties collected by the Board totals $45,000.
This bill would also increase the administrative obligations of: (1) the Board to consult with the
Alabama Commission on Evaluation Services (ACES) to develop performance metric data and
other measures of success to include in their annual reporting requirements established pursuant
to this bill; and (2) ACES to conduct an evaluation of the program during the 2028 fiscal year.
